name: ENKI Precision Tier Vocabulary Pack
description: Universal precision tiers shared across every property in the substrate. When a source asserts a value, the substrate records WHICH precision tier the assertion sits at — `named` ('red'), `qualified` ('candy red'), `formal` ('Pantone 199C'), `spectral` ('λ=620nm'). The collapse operator uses these tiers to merge assertions about the same property cleanly: deeper subsumes shallower, alternatives at the same depth flag as conflicts. Federation uses them to merge across nodes deterministically — the deepest assertion wins, the shallower ones become supporting attestations. Forward-compat: new tiers extend at the bottom of the lattice (higher depths) and never renumber existing ones. v0.1.0: 6 base tiers (concept, named, qualified, formal, spectral, enumerated).

metadata.author: ENKI System
forward_compat_rules: Existing tier depths are immutable. v0.2.0 cannot renumber 'named' from depth=1.
New tiers are added at the END of the depth scale (higher depths) OR as named extensions of existing tiers.
Tiers cannot be removed within a major version — only deprecated with a 'replaced_by' pointer.
